population_method: Validation study of MTLD, vocd-D and HD-D on language samples
finding: MTLD was evaluated as a length-robust lexical-diversity measure
limitation: Not passive smartphone typing or cognitive decline.

citation: Covington & McFall (2010), Journal of Quantitative Linguistics
finding: Moving windows reduce the length dependence of ordinary TTR
limitation: Requires enough observed tokens and does not solve snapshot reconstruction bias.

citation: Vizer et al. (2020), Frontiers in Digital Health
population_method: MCI vs healthy controls using natural-language and touchscreen-typing features
finding: Lexical richness/repetition and typing features contributed to classification
limitation: Spontaneous text processing still requires reliable text tokens; not equivalent to this SensorDB snapshot schema.

citation: Kampman et al. (2022), Multiple Sclerosis Journal: Experimental, Translational and Clinical
population_method: Longitudinal passive smartphone keystroke dynamics in 102 people with MS
finding: Timing features were associated with arm function and processing speed
limitation: Used true keystroke metadata, so timing is not directly comparable to text-state snapshots.

population_method: 21 older adults with one year of passive multimodal smartphone sensing
finding: Preliminary typing variability differences separated cognitively normal from MCI/dementia participants
limitation: Conference abstract, small cohort, and keystroke measures differ from this text-state database.

citation: Petriglia et al. (2025), Research Methods in Medicine & Health Sciences, 4:100276
finding: Age-related lexical-diversity decline varied by metric; MATTR/MTLD effects were smaller or inconsistent
limitation: Language samples, not passive typing; supports metric caution rather than a clinical claim.
